## Circular to deemed licensed corporations 1 which have not submitted migration applications

## Client assets arrangement in anticipation of business cessation

This circular aims to provide guidance to certain deemed licensed corporations (which will not  lodge  their  migration  applications  by  31  January  2005)  about  the  arrangements  they should make regarding client assets.

As mentioned in our circular of 21 October 2004, should you fail to lodge your migration application by the end of the transitional period (i.e. 31 March 2005), your existing licence to conduct regulated activities will automatically cease to have effect.

## Return or transfer of client assets

If you do not intend migrating, you should consider winding down your business and making early preparation for the return or transfer of client assets under your custody.

In  this  connection,  we  would  expect  you  to  adopt  a  proactive  approach  in  contacting  your clients, notifying them of your intention to cease business and seeking their instructions as to whether  they  wish  to  collect  their  assets  or  transfer  them  to  another  intermediary.    Your attention  is  drawn  to  section  6  of  the  Securities  and  Futures  (Client  Securities)  Rules  and section 5 of the Securities and Futures (Client Money) Rules and the circumstances in which the client's written direction is required before the licensed corporation is permitted to deal with the client's assets.

Since it takes time to get in touch with all clients, you should take the necessary actions as early as practicable before your licence expires.

1 Deemed licensed corporations refer to firms which were registered or licensed under the repealed Securities Ordinance, Commodities Trading Ordinance or Leveraged Foreign Exchange Trading Ordinance immediately before 1 April 2003 and are now deemed to have been licensed under the Securities and Futures Ordinance pursuant to the transitional provisions contained therein.

## Treatment of unclaimed client assets

Before your licence expires, you should make every practical effort to contact your clients and to deal with their assets in accordance with their instructions. Where some of your clients cannot  be  contacted,  we  would  expect  you  to  post  notices  in  newspapers  regarding  your business cessation plan (setting out the timeframe and the actions expected of your clients).

Despite  your  efforts,  there  may  be  unclaimed  client  assets.    We  consider  that  you  will continue to owe fiduciary duties to your former clients in respect of such unclaimed client assets even after the expiry of your licence.  You are advised to seek professional advice on the most  appropriate  way  to  deal  with  unclaimed  client  assets.    This  may  involve consideration of an application under the Trustee Ordinance.

In appropriate cases, the Commission may consider exercising its power under section 205 of the Securities and Futures Ordinance to issue a notice requiring a licensed corporation to deal with client assets in a specified manner.

## Bi-weekly status report

If  you  do  not  lodge  your  migration  application by 31  January  2005 ,  you  should  submit a report containing your client assets position on a bi-weekly basis.  In the report, you need to detail:

- (a) the aggregate amount of cash held by you for clients;
- (b) the aggregate value of securities held by you for clients;
- (c) the aggregate value of client assets held by you other than items (a) and (b) above;
- (d) the number of clients concerned;
- (e) the breakdown of the positions of the top 20 clients in terms of asset size; and
- (f) the steps taken / to be taken to contact your clients and notify them of your cessation of business (if you do not intend migrating).

Until your licence expires or is revoked, you should submit the above report to the Licensing Department  of  the  SFC  for  positions  as  of  the  1 st and  the  15 th of  each  month  within  the following two weeks. The  first  report  for  positions  as  of  15  January  2005  should  be submitted by 29 January 2005.

Should you have any questions, please contact your Intermediaries Relationship Manager of the Licensing Department.

Licensing Department Intermediaries and Investment Products Division Securities and Futures Commission
